svg.text: Corn-ethanol additives for livestock, then novel protein for pets
Every notice to FDA's animal-food GRAS programme, grouped by who the ingredient is for. Above each line, notices FDA cleared; below,
notices the company pulled. Rows share one scale, so height is notices per year — a taller row really is a busier one.
The bar on the right is the same rows' outcomes as shares. Pets clear more and pull less than livestock; claiming both at once is the worst row on the chart.
pets AND livestock in one notice
Pets clear 60% and pull 15%. Food-producing clears 53% and pulls 35%. Claiming pets AND livestock in one notice clears 20% and pulls 70%.
That last row is 10 notices, so read it as a warning rather than a rate — but it points the same way as the species count does: notices naming 1–3 species clear 54%,
those naming four or more clear 41%, and that gap survives dropping the ethanol cohort (55/45) and everything before 2018 (55/43).
Gaussian kernel, bandwidth 1.1 years, area scaled to counts rather than normalised. 94 notices over 16 years — every row is thin, and the printed counts are the honest version
of each curve. Species groups are read off FDA's intended-species text. Source: FDA animal food GRAS inventory, agras-notices-2026-09-11.html.
